nodes.label: Demo run sheet — 15 minutes, live, resettable
Fixture timing rule — event start = now + 180 min
nodes.rationale: Registration closes unconditionally once the check-in window opens (start − 60 min, G11), so the registration-open window is exactly (offset − 60) min wide. A 45-min offset opened the event already past that boundary; 90 min left a window this prep block consumes. 180 min leaves ~120 min that outlasts prep plus the 15-min demo.

nodes.label: Registration and self-serve check-in windows are disjoint by design
nodes.rationale: No offset makes live registration (Beat 3) and a self-serve Beat 4 both work at the same wall-clock moment. The old script only worked because self_check_in's time guard was missing until DEFERRED 57 closed. Options left open: seed a second already-live event, or build walk-in registration (a real product question, not a demo hack).

nodes.label: Karen Lau's check-in is single-use — do not spend it in prep
nodes.rationale: The automatic credit posts only on her first transition to attended. Test-scanning her pass, or running ledger-demo.ts (whose step 3 checks her in through a direct RPC that bypasses the Server Action), both silently spend it — Beat 4.6 then returns empty with no error anywhere. Recover by re-seeding or with reconcile-event.ts.

nodes.label: Beat 4.6 — CPD credit logs itself on check-in
nodes.rationale: credit_earned / attendance_verified / 3 hours / HKAM posts itself the instant her check-in resolves to a real account plus a verified licence. The other five attendees have no licence and correctly post nothing — a real guard, not a gap. Posts hours with points and category empty (config-free issuance), which sets up the contrast with Beat 5.

nodes.label: Beat 5 — the trust moment (ledger-demo.ts)
nodes.rationale: Check-in → credit entry with chain hash → live UPDATE rejected (42501) → simulated tamper → verify_ledger_chain() flags the exact row. Uses a different practitioner (organiser_attested tier) so the tamper never touches Beat 4.6's real automatic record.

nodes.label: Demo reset procedure (reset-demo.ts)
nodes.rationale: Reset regenerates every registration code, so render-emails.ts must be re-run after each reset. Never run demo flows against live Seoul/Singapore — credit_ledger is append-only, so demo rows would be permanent residue in a regulator-facing table; enforced by a hard localEnv() guard.
